tips.comment: The model I run suggests Jack To Bat can win this ahead of Buckna in second and Rock On Cowboy in third. This result has largely been driven by Jack To Bat having the highest RPR of the field and the second highest OR. Every runner here is carrying the same weight.

Ceolwulf was placed at Sedgefield and Leicester in February before finally winning at the 11th attempt over 2m4f here at Warwick last month. He should improve for the step up to 3 miles, and just 4lbs higher looks a good bet to follow up.

Pulled up at Taunton after a wind op, but absolutely destroyed his opponent at Fakenham last time out by a clear five lengths after a 56-day break. Should fire even stronger this time out and hasn't been punished for that win.

Still a maiden after 20 runs over jumps, but he has been in decent form of late with a couple of places and is well treated in this. Could get another place and maybe a win in what seems to be an ordinary-looking lineup.

Just 1 point win to date. Although he finished 4th at Hereford 2 weeks ago, not far behind, it seems the quest for his first win under Rules may take a little longer. However, with the talented Jack Quinlan in the saddle, a place finish looks highly likely. Betting each-way at 16/1 could yield a good return.

This lad is 3lb worse off than when he returned with a win at Fontwell last time out, but that was from a 4-month break. He has won twice previously under this today's turnaround. Chadwick may be challenged by Beau Morgan for the lead, but he usually finds a way to beat himself anyway. Coming on from that last win, the circumstances of the race are in place for Hecouldbetheone.

the model I run suggests Six And Out can win this one. There are plenty of options in what looks like a tight race but at 23s this feels like the value bet. There are 3 places on offer so each way might be appealing depending on your betting style. Six And Out has the second highest RPR of the field but steps out with a massive weight advantage, carrying c. 15 lbs less than the top of the market. This race also represents a drop in trip from Class 3 to Class 4.

The model I run simulates this race and has Gwennie May Jem to come in first ahead of Superstylin in second and El Rojo Grande in third. This result has largely been driven by Gwennie May Jem having the joint highest RPR of the field, but a mid-range official rating which leaves her with a decent weight to carry. This horse has placed plenty but is yet to get over the line first in recent races, and maybe this can be the right opportunity to do that. Tristan Durrell on board also takes off 3 lbs.

Won on last 2 visits here, and the form of the win last time looks decent with the mare Minnimum in 3rd, hosing up over fences last week at Cheltenham from 8 lbs higher. Ran well from this mark in a class 2 Pertemps qualifier when 5th at Chepstow LTO. Calmer waters here.

I was on Snipe 12 days ago but he unfortunately fell in the Scottish National. Reverts to the smaller obstacles off of 5lb lower than his chase mark and with a 3lb claim his is 8lb lower now hurdling. Has form around Warwick and should find this slightly easier than recent races.

Lightly 7yo. He has got his act together recently, only beaten 2L last month. Three weeks ago, he had the field strung out when winning by a cozy 6L. Higher mark in this handicap, but he is looking progressive.

Sits 3lbs below his last winning mark. With a 3lbs claiming jockey onboard. Essentially making him 6lbs below that last winning mark. Admittedly he comes into this with a bit to prove at present. His mark has dropped from 116 to 108 however. He's got ground conditions in his favour. And we know this track suits him. He ran a cracker over CD off this mark last season. Finishing a very close 2nd behind Trapista. Beaten just a neck. That horse franked the form, winning again off a 7lbs higher mark nto. He also placed off an 8lbs higher mark than this. Finishing 2nd behind Parisencore in the Bet365 Perth Silver Cup. A repeat of that form here would give him decent claims in this field.

Didn’t have the pace to challenge when going third 4 out and a beaten favourite over 2 furlongs less at Fontwell last month. Drops 3 pounds in the ratings as a consequence and will welcome the extra 2 furlongs today.

The model I run suggests Kayce Dutton can get over the line first here. This horse has the second highest RPR of the field, and a comparable official ranking to the top of the market. Has come second 4 times in the last 5 races so plenty of form.
Big Boy Barney made a favourable impression on racecourse debut, finishing a fair fourth behind a couple of nice horses. Looking for a confidence booster here before he goes hurdling.

The model I run suggests Pioneer Pete can win this race. Steps out with the second highest RPR of the field, but most horses here at the top of the market are carrying the same weight over this 2m NHF. Prior Warwick 2m run came second and looks to get the nose in front first here this time.

Double Tiger looks interesting in this good looking bumper. He is by Blue Bresil who is producing plenty of winners and he is out of a family known very well to the trainer, which goes back to Gold Cup winner Long Run. The trainer, Robert Waley-Cohen may not be a familiar name, but he is very well known in the Point-to-Point sphere and was a very good amateur rider himself. The amateur jockey James King has been booked and he is one of the best amateur riders around.
Tropical Dancer, a 2-year-old colt, trained by K Ryan and ridden by T Eaves, is making his debut here. He is well drawn in stall 1. Worth an interest at around 6/1.

The Ed Bethell-trained Haberdash fluffed his lines last time out after being well-backed but missed the break badly and was always adrift, outpaced on debut at Pontefract. The 5f here at Beverley is probably the biggest draw bias in the country. Quite simply, low-drawn runners here over 5 furlongs have a massive advantage. Haberdash is drawn in 2, which could signal another gamble.

A Mayson colt, whose dam had a brief stint in France and is half-sister to the successful 2-year-old winner Princesse De Saba. As one of 2 debutants from the stable, this 2-year-old is set to be ridden by the skilled Craig Lidster, who has been riding impressively. With odds at 33/1, this colt offers an enticing each-way betting prospect.

South Parade was progressive throughout last year, winning at Thirsk in August. After being placed in her next three starts, she won at Musselburgh in October. She starts this season from a 5 lbs higher mark but is well drawn and can go in again.

Finished last from six over today's trip on the AW at Chelmsford in February but improved to win over the same trip at Doncaster twenty five days ago. Has now won one and placed in three of her last five starts. Should be thereabouts.

Has reserved all her best form for Beverley and has won here 3 times. Although not run since August, she won on seasonal debut last year over course and distance. Should be ready for today, and the 8/1 on offer looks too big.

The 5-year-old made a debut for a new yard last month after coming off a 5-month break. He was beaten just a neck in an 11-runner AW handicap despite not much going right for him in that race. Something to build on.

A drop in class on seasonal debut can pay dividends for Burning Cash. Off since July but had been running well at a higher level and won last May on his last effort at this level from a mark of 81. Same mark here today and looks well drawn in stall 2 with front runners in 1 and 3. Went well on reappearance last year, finishing a close 2nd, and the yard had their first winner in a while yesterday so could be hitting some form.

A winner and a close-up third on his two prior visits to this track. He ran well on his debut for this yard but not as well the other times, but those all took his AW record to 0/6. He should do better now on turf and perhaps back at this track.

A very competitive-looking sprint where 10/1 shot 'High Opinion' looks great value. When last seen, he was contesting a Class 2 handicap (Class 4 today) and wasn't far away. He races off a lower mark today, and this stiff course should suit.

DIGITAL doesn't have the best of draws, but has now had a run out to blow away the cobwebs and drops to two pounds below his last winning mark. That reappearance run was a little better than expected too, and peak turf form last season was in a higher grade and weight, so there's probably going to be an uptick at some stage if returning to that sort of form. Let's hope it's whilst the price is in our favor.

Project Dante won off a 67 back in September and last month returned at the back of the pack after a break, as he has done every race after a break. Worth another shot off today's mark of 68, and because of the wide draw, only Each Way 4P.

I'm going to take a swing on this bottom weight here with the blinkers going back on after being left off for his seasonal debut run last time out, which was no more than an exercise in blowing away the cobwebs. He's slipped to a career-low handicap mark now, and we know that 5 furlongs on decent ground is what he needs. His last 3 turf wins were under those conditions off 71, 60, and 65. He races here off 66 with the jockey claiming 5lb, and the horse's 2 placed efforts over C&D were when chasing home 90+ rated horses. So clearly, the ability is there if he has a going day.
Related to some good winners. Good pedigree on paper for top yard. Yard in good form recently with a 62% win/place strike rate over the past two weeks. Should be involved at the finish.

Was not able to make an impression in debut run when 7 of 7 at Southwell last month. No doubt that performance has contributed to a massive price tomorrow, but the sire (Belardo (IRE)) has a better than average strike rate, so anything is possible.

Could not really get going in debut run when 9th of 12 at Newcastle last month. Sometimes, a switch from AW to turf can be beneficial, and it helps that the sire, Postponed (IRE), is in profit in the last 28 days.
Hyperchromatic shaped well on seasonal return at Newbury and looks like he’ll come on plenty for that. His mark’s no gift just yet, but he’s open to progress and should be sharper now.

Territorial Knight could be worth a go as he won a C4 novice back in July. He then had two duff runs in C2 and then listed company, but returns today after being gelded and having wind surgery in an easier C4. I think the yard expects more today as they have Kevin Stott on top to help out.

Still not won on six starts (two on turf) but wasn't beaten far when finishing second over today's trip at Southwell last month when returning from almost five months off. Should be fitter today. Should be involved at the finish.

Two Be Tanned had been unplaced in her first 6 starts, but cheekpieces seemed to bring great improvement when she won over course and distance at 25/1 last week. She won easily by 3.5 lengths and must have a great chance of overcoming the 5 lbs penalty.
Waiting for room and ran on to be nearest at the finish over 7 furlongs at Southwell at the weekend and will welcome the extra furlong and a half.

Five career runs for the 4-year-old. Just average last year in four races, but a few winners have come out of those races. He returned last month after 8 months off the track, only 9th of 21 runners. A few runners from the race have run well since, but he started slowly, still at the rear entering the final furlong but stayed on nicely. Possibly better than the actual stats as all the action was on the far side and he raced up the near side. Something to build on, facing much lower-rated rivals now and has a 3lb lower mark.

Switches back to turf after two poor runs, but it looks like those runs were on purpose as he ran a blinder the time before, finishing with VOLENTI and EDEN STORM over this trip at Newcastle. Now switched back to turf with blinkers applied, it could be a nice Easterby plot job here. Best turf run was in a maiden at Ripon, beating SLANEY SWAGGER by 5 lengths which is decent form and has improved since. will stay all day and David Allen is top class

The trainer has hit form now with his small string, and he's always been a good placer of horses in handicaps. This 20/1 outsider has been placed in 2 of his 3 runs over C&D, which is especially important around this tricky course. One of those was on similarly fast ground when only going down by half a length off the same mark, so it's easy enough to suggest that this 20/1 quote is way too big, especially now that the trainer's horses are performing better.
Runner-up here last year over C&D off a mark 13lb higher than today. Underwhelming since, but will pick up at some point with a tumbling mark. Worth a go at this price that it's today.

Alfie Boy travelled like the winner for a long way at Redcar and should strip fitter for that comeback. He’s yet to convince over a mile, but both tries came on testing ground. With better conditions and a sharp track, he’s got every chance for a trainer who does well here.

Hostelry has found another excellent opportunity to gain another victory back to back after a good win at Nottingham 12 days ago the handicapper has raised her 4lb as a result as is now operating on a mark 57 however that is of no concern and she still figures on a very handy mark here and she was denied a clear run at a crucially stage last time out before the final 2 furlong but did very well under the circumstances to eventually win by 1.25 lengths and did hit the line with real promise and could of easily won by a bigger margin if granted a clearer passage at that crucial stage so a 4lb rise should be of no concern and Mrs R Carr's mare is likely to remain very competitive this class 6 handicap is pretty thin in nature and Hostelry can make the most of this straightforward looking assignment jockey Kaiya Fraser takes of a handy 3lb which can help her cause here with ground conditions also in Hostelry's favour here merits serious consideration
Had not raced for a good while, so the last time out effort when only 8th of 10 at Pontefract hopefully has done him a world of good. He is now helped by a dropped mark and a drop down in class.

It seems fairly obvious to me that this horse's ideal conditions are fast ground and around a mile, which is what she gets here. She's not had that for a long time and has slipped down the handicap accordingly. In fact, the last time the horse had fast ground, she raced over 2 furlongs further and faded, but she was leading at this trip and that was off a 4lb higher mark. The mare clearly is a quirky sort but is just the type to pop up at a price, and the jockey gets on well with her, so perhaps a small win bet at 20/1 is the order of the day.
23 lbs below the Class 3/4 runs on good ground last year. Looks overpriced here and should relish the good ground. Could be a good one. ??'?
A course and distance winner last year and will welcome the drop in trip after racing over a mile and a quarter when 4th of 7 beaten 2 lengths here last week.

Blue Tempus did too much early when last seen but had shown consistency before that and the step up in trip could help him settle and finish better. The jockey booking catches the eye and if he’s fit and ready off the break, he might surprise a few.

Lightly raced daughter of Le Havre & Nette Rousse ( Dam's sire Mastercraftsman ) who was last seen at Wolverhampton making her handicap debut 24 days ago of a mark of 65 where finishing 6th/10 having hung badly right on the bend into the home straight and losing a lot of momentum as a result that was also her return run after a 166 day break and she should strip much fitter and be a lot more alert with that outing under her belt the track here at Beverley should suit Charlie Johnston inmate much better and she is now operating on a slightly reduced mark of 63 and seeing she is still open to plenty of improvement now as a 3yo French Haven can begin to trouble the judge of her current operating mark jockey Joe Fanning takes the ride and can give French Haven the perfect ride here at Beverley considered

Finished just outside the places in fourth over 7f at Newcastle last month but improved to finish third when stepped up to today's trip at Redcar a fortnight ago behind reopposing Salaria (runner up). Should be involved at the finish.

Thrice maiden and hoping similar conditions this out in what will be her handicap debut helps. Also, dropping down in class although up in trip, which might make things tricky, but she has a chance with some improvements.
Magic McColgan had a cracking win in January but could only manage a midfield last month. But that was in a G2, and today is a bit more realistic. Paul is back, who was on top for that last win.

The model I run simulates this race and suggests Mongibello can come in first, ahead of Magic McColgan in second and Visual Impact in third. This result has been largely driven by Mongibello having the highest RPR of the field, the highest official rating in the field, but only having to carry the same weight as Magic McColgan. Mongibello has prior course and distance history under his belt and JJ Slevin picks up the reins.

Ran well in his first run over this trip, flattered by the losing margin to Regent's Stroll but pulled well clear of the rest and the form from his two novice runs prior to that is OK. Yard is in good form and the turnaround time from his last run suits.

The model I run suggests Magnolia can win this one. This price is pretty big, so it offers an each way opportunity if preferable. The jockey on board is Joshua Thompson and takes a further 7 lbs off. This makes the weight difference from the top of the market a total of 23 lbs, which is considerable over a 2m 4f distance trip.

LANGDALE LANE has some smart lines of form and has to be of interest sent to Scotland by his Irish trainer. This yard have been among the recent winners with others running with credit , so with race-sharpness taken on trust on an attractive looking British mark he could get involved.

Raced over 3 miles in Ireland earlier this month, leading for a long way but weakening 2 out and tailed off. That was his second run in a month following an absence of 134 days which he will undoubtedly strip fitter for and the drop in trip could suit.

Jimmy Fyffe owns this Wings Of Eagles sired gelding, and he may have better luck with this one than the mare in the first here yesterday. Mary Stanford was in the thick of the action, then dropped out quickly, being pulled up with blood bleeding from her nose. Baratablet from Nicky Richards' stable should have a very fit horse on their hands, and a big run can be had to give Danny McMenamin a belated birthday present.
Won a novice hurdle in good style when making all and staying on well and hurdling smartly. Makes handicap debut today and could rattle up a few wins before the end of summer.

Decent 3rd place last time out at Ayr with an inexperienced jockey, and having pulled up last time at Kelso. Two wins in two races previous to that, and should show more this time out, being a much improving horse.
Singapore Trip last won when here in May last year off a 110. I think the return here and today's mark of 107 could see him bang in there again.

SAVANT DU MESNIL boasts a strong French sire who produces many classy sorts. This five year old could be a different proposition now handicapping from a modest looking opening mark and the market could reveal more about what is expected today.

Ran well at this meeting last year to finish a close 2nd over two and a half and has won at this longer trip. He has not run that well in his last couple of outings, but a young conditional who has had a couple of winners in the last month comes on and takes 10 lb off. The yard is in good form with a winner here yesterday, and in a mediocre race, he could have a chance.

Hidden History looks good in this Class 3 hurdle at Perth. He quickened up well last time out at Toxxy, beating Wellington Arch who won well at Aintree next time out. 11st 2lbs on his back at Toxxy, this time 10st 12lbs. So handicapper has been very generous and every chance he could go in again.
Won its last race, jockey claiming three pounds, trainer and jockey in good form. Should be there at the business end of the race, a great each way chance at six to one, NAP.

Rambo T won this last year off a 130 and spent the rest of that year chasing with a win off a 134. He has twice returned from a break in the past to win and is worth a shot while on a 133 back hurdling.

Della Casa Lunga drops in grade here after finishing down the field in a Grade 2 hurdle at Doncaster LTO. Prior to that she won well at Kempton when making all from a mark of 134 - that race saw next time out winners in 3rd and 4th so looks plenty strong. Seems at her best on right handed tracks and should appreciate conditions, she can get her nose in front in this Class 3 handicap from just 4lbs higher (138) than her Kempton win.

Heltenham won a G3 off a 130 last March and followed up with a C2 win off a 136. But took on more weight and has been a bit down the pack since. However, returned from a short break last week on a 134 to a decent second and could improve on that today while still running off a 134.

I really like Tommy Oscar, and he has his ground, but twenty furlongs does stretch him. If this was a two miles, I would be all over him. Sean Bowen can get his Perth winner with Doctor Ken, who ran a blinder at Uttoxeter with his first run back, finishing second. He has been given time off to get over the bounce factor that can see Doctor Ken finishing the race off with success.

The model I run suggests Walk On Quest can win this race ahead of Statuario in second and Doctor Ken in third. Walk On Quest has the third highest RPR of the field, but steps out with by far the least weight to carry over the 2m 4f trip. Got pulled last time at Uttoxeter, but if you're willing to overlook that, had prior form figures of 21111.

All 4 career wins for Statuario have been here with 2 of those over course and distance. He has been out of sorts since the most recent win over 3 miles in June 2024 off a mark of 126. Went up to 135 following that win and was high as 140 when racing at Cheltenham in November 2024. Down to a more realistic mark of 127 and could go well at a track he likes.
Cuban Cigar was second in this race last year off 22lb higher in the weights, so looks a value price with conditions to suit the horse too.

Bashful has never raced at Perth, and he could be making his first visit a winning one. He was never involved at Doncaster on the flat, and I would not be surprised if that race was used for a speed test, as they go quicker on the flat than they do over hurdles. He could be showing what he did at Musselburgh and Kelso with winning. He does travel well, and with conditions looking suitable, Charlie Maggs, who takes five pounds off him, can bide his time and come from off the pace with a telling run for success.
Has a nice each way chance in this race. Has trip and ground to suit and jockey gets on well with the horse.

Very disappointing at Fontwell when last in action, so perhaps he is better judged on his run at Wincanton the time before when going right-handed. Handicap debut here for a yard who very rarely have runners at Perth, but they have an excellent record here.

Trailblazer won here last year off a 100 and returns today after a win a couple of weeks ago by 13L. Although taking on 6 lbs for that, he is still only on a 98. We might see more of the same today while keeping Brian in the saddle.
Platin Moon has some fair form on the flat. Looks on a good weight judging on its race last time at Kelso when second of six, which was improved form.

The model I run suggests Belle Of Annandale can win this large field race of 16 runners. Sean Bowen picks up the reins. This horse has by far the highest RPR of the field and a pretty mid-range official ranking, meaning weights being carried are 5-7 lbs shy of the top of the market.

Twice runner-up in similar races last season from 2 lb higher. Has been ticking over well enough on the flat of late, and the return of the visor could well be a plus to him, something he has not worn since February 2024.
I'm a Lumberjack has been found a decent opportunity by Alan King and could take a lot of beating if putting his best hooves forward.
Expected strong pace and upped in trip should suit. Has disappointed the last twice, both in better class races than this, so would have every chance back down in grade.

Konfusion made it 2 wins from 4 when winning very impressively last time after being stepped up to 3 miles. This race is tougher, and he does have the weight burden, but underfoot conditions will suit, and he tackles the 3 miles again today. Judging by his performance last time, it would be no surprise to see him run very close again.

Veteran who landed the Royal Artillery Gold Cup at Sandown on first start since wind surgery when last seen in February. Still on a workable mark for this return to handicap company so should run very well this evening.

A big field allied with a decent pace can get Sam England's free-going 6yo finally off the mark over hurdles, after a run of four seconds. His mark hasn't really moved in that time, and I'm hoping the sound surface can improve him on a third run after a wind-op.

Three runs in a little over five weeks for a mark in November and December. Put away since. Handicap debut here, up in trip and fitted with a tongue strap. Yard appears to be hitting some form, winning with two of their last three runners.

He's still a maiden after 8 career runs, 2 in bumpers and 6 over hurdles, and has been placed twice over hurdles over 16.5f on good and 19.5f on soft. He had an opening handicap mark of 97 three runs ago and was placed over 19.5f two runs ago but runs off a mark of 93 today after a poor run last time out. Trainer D. McCain goes very well here at his local track with his hurdlers, but despite being mob-handed, I'll opt for this one with T. Gillard in the plate.

Two solid efforts in the autumn on soft ground. Not so good at Chepstow over Christmas, but that is not everyone's track. And then again here on by far the quickest ground that he has run on. Back on soft and down a couple of pounds, could be a different proposition now.

Inns Of Fear went close at Newcastle last time and that form looks solid. The step up to 7f should suit based on how he finished off and he showed enough in Ireland to suggest there’s more to come. Looks the standout on paper and the one they’ve all got to beat.
Our nap of the day is Flag of St George, who drops in grade and in weight given by the handicapper and looks well treated on all known form.
Not beaten far when runner-up over course and distance earlier this month. A repeat of that form could get him a ninth career win here.
Ran well to win over today's trip at Southwell in January and followed up with a close second (by a neck) over the same track and trip last month. Should be thereabouts.

Rogue Soldier was impressive when last seen in July and looked like there was more to come off that mark. He hasn’t had much of a go over 7f so there’s a bit to prove on the trip, but if he sees it out, he has a chance to be involved.

Veteran who hasn't won for a while but continues to slip down the weights as a result and showed signs of a revival when 2nd over course and distance last week. Needs to back that up but will surely be striking again soon.

Fat Gladiator clearly needed his comeback run after such a long layoff and actually shaped with a bit of promise that day. He’s now back to 7f, which looks more his thing, and the handicapper’s given him a chance with another 2lb taken off.

Poor debut for new stable on paper, but was in touch with the leaders over the first 7 furlongs before fading. Races over 7f here, having previously won and placed at this course. Seems some value at 40/1.

Merry Minister went mighty close in this race last year and is back on the same mark he won off over 2m, so he’s definitely weighted to go well. He’s been off a while, so fitness is the unknown, but if the yard has him ready, he’s more than capable of getting involved again.
Went second towards the finish over half a furlong shorter here when last seen in February. Remains on the same mark and he is twice a winner over this 14 furlong trip.

Thrice raced daughter of Territories & Firenze ( Dam's sire Efisio ) who hasn't made much of an impact in her trio of novice runs however she makes her handicap debut here of a very attractive mark of 55 and J R Fanshawe's inmate strongly appeals as the type to do much better now heading down the handicap route and is surely bound to be better than a mark 55 in very good time and this looks like the perfect starting point for Castellina the tongue strap is applied for the first time here jockey Kyle Strydom takes the ride and will give this a good shot in good hands capable of taking a big step forward here Castellina must enter calculations

Hala Joza meets some of today's rivals again, better off on the weights despite finishing ahead of them last time when finishing second. She has really improved and has a good profile to step up again and run a big race with Hollie Doyle on board. She does have to overcome an unfavorable draw, but with Hollie doing the steering, a big run is likely, and this filly cannot be dismissed.

SARABI ran better than her 9th of 10 suggests at Lingfield on her stable debut two weeks ago. She actually showed a nice turn of foot about a furlong out before meeting interference and being stopped in her tracks. I think she could have gone close with a clear run. Better drawn here in stall 2, kindly dropped 3lb, with Hector Crouch a talented first-time booking, she looks a decent each way bet.

This is a very poor field; they don't come much worse. I am going for Top Biller as he has already won a race and has run okay in his other starts. He flopped on his first run for this stable but was sent off at a big price, so nothing was obviously expected of him. Could be a different proposition this time at a decent price.
Cavalry Call just looks to be winning soon if you ask me. Just missed out here the run before last and now gets the inside track from the stalls, so should be winning here from this sort of mark.

Fox Avatar was unlucky to find heavy ground in its last race, reason why it could not repeat its successful previous performance at Beverly. Today on this surface, in its handicap debut, it can win again in this company on the hands of de Sousa.
Has hopefully shaken off any rust after 14 months off when 4th of 7 at Newcastle LTO earlier this month. He should welcome the dropped mark, and it helps that he has course experience.

Might be moving in the right direction, especially after the LTO effort when a useful 3rd of 8 at Wolverhampton last month. Still operating below the last winning mark, so hopefully, he can pose a threat tomorrow.

Dr Waksman showed a bit more over hurdles last time and was steadily improving on the Flat before that. Back from a short break and making his handicap debut here, he looks like one who could take a step forward now.
